PROJECT: "[AI-TECH]" — AI & Technology News Platform
## What to build
A modern technology news and tools website covering AI, software, cybersecurity, gadgets,
cloud/hosting, reviews, and how-to guides — combining four traffic engines in one platform:
1. News → search + social traffic
2. SEO guides/reviews → long-term Google traffic
3. Free tools → recurring, sticky traffic independent of news cycles
4. Reviews/comparisons → affiliate revenue

This is explicitly NOT just an "AI news blog" — it is News + AI + Software + Tools +
Reviews combined, because that combination has far more monetization and traffic surface
than a pure news site.

## IMPORTANT — technology reality check
This project requires user accounts, an admin panel, content management, and (optionally)
comments. That means it needs a real backend and database — it CANNOT be a pure static
site like a GitHub-Pages-only project. Use:
- **Frontend/framework**: Next.js (React) — supports SSR/SSG hybrid rendering, which is
  critical for SEO on news content while still allowing dynamic features (login, admin,
  saved articles).
- **Database + auth**: a managed backend such as Supabase or a self-hosted PostgreSQL
  instance with an auth library (e.g., NextAuth/Auth.js) — handles users, roles,
  saved articles, comments.
- **Content storage**: either a headless CMS (e.g., Sanity, Strapi) for articles, or a
  custom admin panel writing directly to the database — build the custom admin panel
  described below since it's a core deliverable, not an afterthought.
- **Hosting**: Vercel (free tier is generous and pairs natively with Next.js) instead of
  GitHub Pages, since this project needs server-side rendering and API routes.
- Confirm this stack with the user before proceeding — if they specifically want to avoid
  any backend/hosting cost, flag that login/admin/comments would need to be scoped down or
  replaced with a third-party embedded service (e.g., a comment widget), and ask which
  trade-off they prefer.

## Visual identity — "beautiful and modern," NOT a generic AI-blog template
Avoid the default AI-generated design clusters (cream background + serif + terracotta
accent; near-black + acid-green/neon accent; broadsheet hairline-rule newspaper layout).
Instead, build a **live broadcast / control-room** aesthetic — appropriate for a site whose
core content is fast-moving tech and AI news:

**Colors:**
- Deep Charcoal Navy `#12131C` — primary dark background
- Paper White `#F7F7F5` — light-mode background / card surfaces on dark mode
- Signal Blue `#3B5BFF` — primary accent (links, primary buttons, active states)
- Broadcast Amber `#FFB020` — secondary accent, used ONLY for "live/breaking/updated" status
  indicators — never as a general decorative color, so it keeps real signaling meaning
- Slate Grey `#8891A6` — secondary text, metadata, timestamps

**Type:**
- Headlines: a bold condensed display face (e.g., Archivo Expanded or Big Shoulders
  Display) — gives headlines weight and urgency appropriate to news
- Body: a clean, highly readable sans (e.g., Inter or Source Sans 3)
- Metadata/code/tool outputs: a monospace face (e.g., IBM Plex Mono) — used for
  timestamps, category tags, and anywhere the developer-tools section shows code/output

**Signature element — status tags:** a small colored dot + label used consistently
throughout the site: `● LIVE`, `● BREAKING`, `● UPDATED 2H AGO`, `● TRENDING`. This is a
structural device that encodes real information (recency/status), not decoration — use it
on homepage cards, article headers, and category pages.

**Secondary motif:** thin circuit-trace-style connecting lines (right-angle, PCB-style)
used sparingly as section dividers or background texture at very low opacity — justified
by the tech/AI subject matter, not a generic hairline rule.

**Layout — homepage hero:** not a single generic "featured article" slab. Build a
**split live-feed hero**: left ~65% width shows the single top breaking story (large image,
headline, live status tag); right ~35% width shows a compact, scrollable "Trending now"
ticker list of 5-6 items with tiny thumbnails and timestamps. This should feel like a live
dashboard, not a static magazine cover.

**Dark mode is the default** (fits the tech/AI audience and the broadcast concept); support
a light-mode toggle using Paper White background with the same accent colors.

**Mobile-first, responsive:** mobile-first design, fast loading, WebP/AVIF images with lazy
loading, minimal blocking JavaScript, must pass Core Web Vitals.

## Site structure & navigation
Top nav: Latest News · Trending · AI · Software · Cybersecurity · Gadgets · Cloud & Hosting
· Reviews · How-To Guides · [search icon] · [language selector 🌍] · Login/Register

Homepage sections (in order): split live-feed hero → Latest News grid → Trending →
category preview rows → newsletter signup block.

## Article page — required elements
- Title, author (with author page link), publish date, last-updated date, featured image
- Body content with headings, tables where relevant, internal links
- Sources section — critical for AI/tech news: **show sources explicitly rather than
  letting AI-generated content pass off unsourced claims as fact**
- Related articles
- Share buttons
- Comments (optional for v1 — can use a lightweight embedded comment service instead of
  building one from scratch)
- Ad placements (defined below)

## Category: AI (flagship category — prioritize this)
Subcategories: AI News · AI Tools · ChatGPT · Claude · Gemini · AI Image Generation ·
AI Video · AI Coding · AI Agents · AI for Business
(Strongest affiliate opportunity on the site — build comparison/"best of" templates for
this category first.)

## Category: Software
Comparison/"best of" article templates for: Best AI Software · Best Productivity Apps ·
Best Video Editors · Best Website Builders · Best SEO Tools · Best Email Marketing
Software · Best Project Management Software
(These convert far better for monetization than plain news — prioritize the template
that supports a comparison table + affiliate links + AdSense in the same layout.)

## Category: Cybersecurity
VPN · Password Managers · Antivirus · Online Privacy · Data Breaches · Security Guides ·
Phishing · Account Security

## Category: Cloud & Hosting
Best Web Hosting · Best Free Hosting · Cloudflare vs Vercel · Vercel vs Netlify · Best VPS
· Cloud Computing · CDN · Domain Guides

## Free Tools section (build these — recurring traffic independent of the news cycle)
SEO Tools: Word Counter · Character Counter · Meta Description Generator · Keyword
Density Checker
Developer Tools: JSON Formatter · JSON Validator · Base64 Encoder/Decoder · URL
Encoder/Decoder · Regex Tester · HTML Formatter · CSS Minifier
AI Tools: AI Prompt Generator · AI Title Generator · AI Meta Description Generator
(Each tool should be a genuinely fast, client-side-computable utility — no paid API calls
— living at a clean URL like /tools/json-formatter/, styled consistently with the rest of
the site so it doesn't feel like a bolted-on afterthought.)

## Internationalization
Build the i18n architecture (routing, translation file structure) to support up to 10
languages (EN, BG, DE, FR, ES, IT, PT, NL, PL, TR), but **launch with English content
only**. Do not generate placeholder translations for the other 9 languages at launch —
add them incrementally once the English site has real traffic, to avoid maintaining 10
versions of every article from day one.

## Login / Register (can be phase 2 if it simplifies the build)
Registered user features: profile · saved articles/bookmarks · reading history ·
newsletter preferences · comments

## Admin panel (core deliverable — build this properly, not as an afterthought)
- **Dashboard**: total articles, total users, total views, today's views, AdSense revenue,
  affiliate revenue — summary cards
- **Articles**: create, edit, delete, draft/publish/schedule, categories, tags, SEO title,
  meta description, featured image upload
- **Users**: view users, ban, delete, change role
- **Analytics**: visitors, pageviews, top articles, countries, devices, traffic sources
- Restrict access to admin/editor roles only, enforced at the auth layer, not just hidden UI

## Monetization (multiple streams, not just AdSense)
1. AdSense — placed below the fold in articles and between homepage sections, never
   adjacent to nav/interactive elements
2. Affiliate marketing — comparison tables in Software/AI/Cloud "best of" articles with
   affiliate links, clearly disclosed
3. Sponsored articles — a distinct visual template/label so they're clearly marked as
   sponsored (required for trust and typically for ad network compliance)
4. Newsletter sponsorships
5. Premium tools — flagged as a phase-2/later feature, not part of MVP

## SEO requirements
- sitemap.xml, robots.txt, canonical URLs
- Open Graph tags on every article
- Structured data: Article schema, Breadcrumb schema
- Author pages, category pages, strong internal linking
- Clean URL structure, e.g.:
  `site.com/ai/best-ai-video-generators`
  `site.com/software/best-seo-tools`
  `site.com/security/best-password-managers`

## Build order
1. **Phase 1 — Core public site**: homepage (live-feed hero), article template, AI +
   Software categories with 3-5 real articles each, one "best of" comparison template
   with affiliate table support, 3 tools from the Free Tools section, SEO fundamentals
   (sitemap, schema, OG tags), fully responsive, dark mode default.
2. **Phase 2 — Admin panel + auth**: login/register, roles, the full admin panel described
   above (dashboard, article CRUD, user management, analytics), so content can be managed
   without touching code.
3. **Phase 3 — Remaining categories & tools**: Cybersecurity, Gadgets, Cloud & Hosting,
   Reviews, How-To Guides categories; remaining tools (JSON/Base64/Regex/etc.); newsletter
   signup + sponsorship placement; comments (embedded service or custom).
4. **Phase 4 — i18n expansion**: add languages incrementally once traffic data shows which
   markets matter most.

## Deliverables expected
- Full project repo structure ready to deploy to Vercel (or the confirmed hosting choice).
- Clean, commented code; database schema documented.
- README.md with local setup, environment variables needed, and deploy instructions.
- Confirm site name, primary domain, and hosting/budget constraints with the user before
  writing code. Build Phase 1 completely before moving to Phase 2.

---
title: Deploying Next.js to different platforms
nav_title: Deploying to Platforms
description: Understand which Next.js features require specific platform capabilities and how to choose the right deployment target.
related:
  description: Related guides and references.
  links:
    - app/guides/rendering-philosophy
    - app/guides/self-hosting
    - app/getting-started/deploying
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath
---

Next.js [treats static and dynamic content as a spectrum](/docs/app/guides/rendering-philosophy) at the component level. Different features in this model require different platform capabilities. This page helps you understand what your platform needs to support and how to configure your deployment.

## Minimum Requirements

To run Next.js, your platform needs **a Node.js server**. That's it.

A single `next start` process handles every Next.js feature correctly: Server Components, ISR, PPR, Cache Components, Server Actions, Proxy, and `after()`. Streaming support is needed for features like PPR and Server Components to deliver content progressively (without it, responses are buffered and sent as a whole, which still works but loses the streaming performance benefit). Additional infrastructure (CDN caching, edge compute, shared cache) primarily improves performance and multi-instance consistency. In multi-instance deployments, shared cache and tag coordination reduce stale divergence between instances. The only additional dependency is the `sharp` package, which is required for [Image Optimization](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image).

## Functional Fidelity vs. Performance Fidelity

When evaluating platform support for Next.js, it helps to distinguish between two levels:

**Functional fidelity** means every Next.js feature works correctly. The [adapter test suite](/docs/app/api-reference/adapters/testing-adapters) is the contract: if a platform's adapter passes the tests, it supports Next.js. This is binary: it passes or it doesn't.

**Performance fidelity** means features achieve their optimal performance characteristics. Examples include PPR's static shell served at CDN latency rather than origin latency, or ISR serving stale content instantly with sub-second revalidation propagation. Performance fidelity is a spectrum that every platform will achieve differently based on their architecture.

A platform that achieves functional fidelity is a fully supported deployment target for Next.js. Performance fidelity is how platforms differentiate, and it improves incrementally over time.

Use the feature matrix below through this lens: "Streaming Required" and "Shared Cache Recommended" describe what is needed for functional fidelity. "Edge Stitching" is a performance fidelity optimization.

## Feature Support Matrix

Different features require different infrastructure capabilities. The "Edge Stitching" column is a **performance optimization**, not a correctness requirement. All features work correctly from a single origin server.

| Feature                        | Streaming | Shared Cache | Edge Stitching | Notes                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------ | --------- | ------------ | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Server Components              | Required  | No           | No             | Basic streaming support                                                                          |
| ISR (time-based)               | No        | Recommended  | No             | Works per-instance without shared cache                                                          |
| ISR (on-demand)                | No        | Recommended  | No             | [Tag propagation](/docs/app/guides/how-revalidation-works) needs shared cache for multi-instance |
| Partial Prerendering           | Required  | Recommended  | Optional       | [See PPR Platform Guide](/docs/app/guides/ppr-platform-guide)                                    |
| Cache Components (`use cache`) | Required  | Recommended  | No             | Shared cache enables cross-instance consistency                                                  |
| Proxy / Middleware             | No        | No           | No             | Runs at edge or origin                                                                           |
| Server Actions                 | Required  | No           | No             | POST requests with streaming response                                                            |
| `after()`                      | No        | No           | No             | Requires [graceful shutdown](/docs/app/guides/self-hosting#after) support                        |

**Streaming Required** means the platform must support chunked transfer encoding or HTTP/2 streaming and must not buffer the response before sending it to the client.

**Shared Cache Recommended** means multiple server instances benefit from shared cache backends to coordinate. For ISR and server response caching, use [`cacheHandler`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/incrementalCacheHandlerPath). For `'use cache'` entries, use [`cacheHandlers`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers). Without shared cache, each instance maintains its own cache independently �?" features still work correctly on each instance, but revalidation events don't propagate across instances.

## CDN Infrastructure Compatibility

The following table maps infrastructure primitives for each major CDN. These are available building blocks, not finished integrations:

| CDN               | Edge Compute | Key-Value / Tags | Blob Storage   | PPR Resuming |
| ----------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | -------------- | ------------ |
| Cloudflare        | Workers      | KV               | R2             | Yes (worker) |
| Akamai            | EdgeWorkers  | EdgeKV           | Object Storage | Yes (worker) |
| Amazon CloudFront | Lambda@Edge  | KeyValueStore    | S3             | Yes (Lambda) |
| Fastly            | Compute      | KV Store         | Object Storage | Yes (WASM)   |
| Azure             | Functions    | Managed Redis    | Blob Storage   | Yes (server) |
| Google Cloud      | Cloud Run    | Various KV       | Cloud Storage  | Yes (server) |

These are available building blocks, not finished integrations. Additional infrastructure (CDN caching, edge compute, shared cache) primarily improves performance and multi-instance consistency. In multi-instance deployments, shared cache and tag coordination reduce stale divergence between instances. The only additional dependency is the `sharp` package, which is required for [Image Optimization](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image).

When evaluating platform support for Next.js, it helps to distinguish between two levels:

**Functional fidelity** means every Next.js feature works correctly. The [adapter test suite](/docs/app/api-reference/adapters/testing-adapters) is the contract: if a platform's adapter passes the tests, it supports Next.js. This is binary: it passes or it doesn't.

**Performance fidelity** means features achieve their optimal performance characteristics. Examples include PPR's static shell served at CDN latency rather than origin latency, or ISR serving stale content instantly with sub-second revalidation propagation. Performance fidelity is a spectrum that every platform will achieve differently based on their architecture.

A platform that achieves functional fidelity is a fully supported deployment target for Next.js. Performance fidelity is how platforms differentiate, and it improves incrementally over time.

OK, Cloudflare has its own Next.js integration (`@opennextjs/cloudflare`). For Phase 1, since content is static data, the site will be fully static at build time (generateStaticParams). That works great on Cloudflare Pages with OpenNext, which I'll configure in Phase 2 setup with wrangler. For now, I'll build the app so it works as standard Next.js.

Let me now start building. First the design system and globals.css.

Let me plan the file structure:

```
src/
  app/
    layout.tsx
    page.tsx                    — homepage
    globals.css
    not-found.tsx
    sitemap.ts
    robots.ts
    ai/page.tsx                 — AI category
    software/page.tsx           — Software category
    security/page.tsx           — (Phase 3, stub?) — skip for Phase 1, but nav has Cybersecurity... The brief Phase 1 says AI + Software categories only. Nav can include links but pages for others could be "coming soon"? Better to keep nav to what exists in Phase 1: Latest News, Trending, AI, Software, Reviews(best-of). Hmm. The brief site structure lists all categories in nav. But Phase 1 builds AI + Software. I'll include all nav items, with unbuilt categories 404ing? That's bad UX. 

    Decision: Nav shows all 8 categories per the brief. For Phase 1, I'll build AI, Software fully. For Cybersecurity, Gadgets, Cloud & Hosting, Reviews, How-To Guides — I'll create simple category pages listing "coming soon" or, better, include them in the nav but they render a category page shell with empty state. Actually simplest clean approach: build a generic category page component driven by data; categories without articles show a nice empty state "More coverage coming soon". That keeps structure clean and nav functional without 404s.
    
    Actually — I have limited time but can seed a few articles for Cybersecurity/Cloud too? The brief Phase 1 says AI + Software categories with 3-5 real articles each, one best-of template. Let me focus: AI (4 articles incl. 1 best-of "Best AI video generators"), Software (4 articles incl. 1 best-of "Best SEO tools"). I'll build category pages for all categories generically; non-seeded ones show empty state.
    
    blog/[slug]/page.tsx        — article
    author/[slug]/page.tsx      — author
    category/[slug]/page.tsx    — generic category (AI, Software can also use this; simpler than separate files)
    tools/
      layout.tsx
      page.tsx                  — tools index
      word-counter/page.tsx
      character-counter/page.tsx
      meta-description-generator/page.tsx
    admin/                      — Phase 2 (auth-protected) — scaffold
      layout.tsx
      page.tsx                  — dashboard
    api/                        — Phase 2 route handlers scaffold
  components/
    ...
  lib/
    ...
  content/
    articles/*.mdx  — or TS data?
```

For content: MDX requires extra deps (`next-mdx-remote` or the built-in MDX support). Next has built-in MDX support via `@next/mdx` but that's legacy-ish; Next 16 docs list a `mdx.md` guide. Actually for a content layer that Phase 2 will replace with a database, plain structured TS data (content in TypeScript files) is simplest, zero extra deps, fully typed, and easy to swap for DB fetch. Given articles have rich content (headings, tables, sources), I can model body as an array of block objects (paragraph, h2, h3, table, list, callout, quote, affiliateBlock) and render them. That's clean, typed, no MDX parsing. And it maps directly to how a CMS/DB would store it (block content). I'll go with structured TS data — it also makes the "best-of" affiliate table a first-class data structure.

This is the pragmatic, robust choice. Let me design the content model:

```ts
type ContentBlock =
  | { type: "p"; text: string }
  | { type: "h2"; text: string }
  | { type: "h3"; text: string }
  | { type: "ul"; items: string[] }
  | { type: "ol"; items: string[] }
  | { type: "quote"; text: string; cite?: string }
  | { type: "callout"; tone: "info"|"warn"|"success"; title?: string; text: string }
  | { type: "table"; columns: string[]; rows: string[][] }
  | { type: "affiliate"; ... } // comparison row
  | { type: "image"; ... }
```

Article type:
```ts
type Status = "live" | "breaking" | "updated" | "trending";
type Article = {
  slug: string;
  title: string;
  excerpt: string;

parts.text:
Now let me also fix the search index to include category already (it does). Good.

Now update todo status and build the root layout. Layout needs:
- Fonts: Big_Shoulders_Display, Inter, IBM_Plex_Mono via next/font/google
- Theme init script (inline) to set .light before paint from localStorage
- metadata: title template, description, metadataBase, OG defaults, icons
- viewport export (themeColor)

Next 16: `viewport` export from layout. Let me check the docs quickly for `viewport` — standard: `export const viewport: Viewport = { themeColor: "#12131C", colorScheme: "dark" }`.

For the inline theme script in <head>, I'll use a <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML> in the head? Next.js recommends placing in <head> via <script>. I'll add it to body top or head. In Next app router, you can render <script> in the layout body before content. Let me place a <script> right after <body> opening tag with the theme logic.

Inline script:
```js
(function(){try{var t=localStorage.getItem("aitech-theme");if(t==="light")document.documentElement.classList.add("light");}catch(e){}})();
```

Also add `<script>` for no-flash. Fine.

metadataBase: use siteConfig.url.

Let me write layout.tsx.
Now the root layout with fonts, theme bootstrap, and metadata.

Now the homepage (app/page.tsx). Sections:
1. Hero (split live-feed)
2. CircuitDivider
3. Latest News grid (SectionHeading "Latest News" kicker "The news cycle" + link /news) — grid of remaining articles (exclude featured) — maybe 6 cards.
4. AdSlot between sections
5. Trending → the hero already has trending. The brief says homepage sections: hero → Latest News grid → Trending → category preview rows → newsletter. Hmm the hero already includes "Trending now" ticker on the right. The separate "Trending" section could be a fuller trending list. To avoid duplication, I'll make the "Trending" section a horizontal row of trending cards (4) with the ticker staying in the hero. Actually let me follow brief order: after Latest grid, a "Trending" section with a strip of trending articles (compact horizontal cards showing rank). Then category preview rows (AI, Software). Then newsletter block.

6. Newsletter block (The Signal)
7. AdSlot at bottom.

Let me build homepage with sub-components inline. I'll import from content.

The "Trending" section: horizontal scroll row of compact cards with big rank numbers.

Let me write page.tsx.
Now the homepage with the split live-feed hero and all sections.

Now the article page: `app/[category]/[slug]/page.tsx`. Required elements:
- Title, author (with author page link), publish date, last-updated date, featured image
- Body with headings, tables, internal links
- Sources section
- Related articles
- Share buttons
- Ad placements
- Status tag
- Breadcrumbs
- Structured data: Article + Breadcrumb schema (JSON-LD)
- metadata: title, description, OG, canonical
- Sponsored label if sponsored
- Affiliate disclosure + comparison table if affiliate.catalog

Layout: two-column: main article column (max-w ~ 760px centered or with sidebar). I'll do: container max-w-[1440px]; grid with article content column (max-w-3xl) + right sidebar (related + newsletter mini + ad). Sidebar hidden on mobile.

generateStaticParams: return all (category, slug) pairs from articles.

Also `generateMetadata({ params })` — params is Promise.

For notFound when category/slug invalid → notFound().

JSON-LD: Article schema with headline, image, datePublished, dateModified, author, publisher. Breadcrumb schema.

Let me also add author link: `/author/[slug]`.

Let me write the article page. I need to compute canonical URL: `${siteConfig.url}/${category}/${slug}`.

Related articles: getRelatedArticles(article) — but those may be from different category; links use `/${related.category}/${related.slug}`.

Also handle "updated" tag: if updatedAt, show "Last updated {date}" and the UPDATED status tag.

Article meta bar: author avatar + name link, published date, updated date, reading time, share buttons on the right.

Hero image: CoverArt full width aspect video with credit overlay.

Let me write it.
Now the article template — the core page with all required elements and structured data.

Now the category page: `app/[category]/page.tsx`. Shows:
- Category header: name (display), description, topic chips, article count, live status
- Breadcrumbs
- Article grid (all in category)
- Ad slot
- Newsletter mini at bottom
- JSON-LD CollectionPage/ItemList? Optional. I'll add Breadcrumb schema.

generateStaticParams: return category slugs (all 7, even empty ones — they show empty state).

generateMetadata: title `${category.name} News & Guides`, description from category.description, canonical.

If category invalid → notFound.

Let me write it.
Now the category page (also serves the AI/Software flagship sections).

Now the aggregate pages: /news and /trending, plus author page /author/[slug].

/news: SectionHeading "Latest News", grid of all articles sorted desc.
/trending: ranked list with big numbers.

Let me create app/news/page.tsx and app/trending/page.tsx.

Then author page.

Then not-found, tools, misc pages (login/register/about/privacy/terms/affiliate-disclosure), sitemap, robots, OG image.

Let me write news and trending pages.
Aggregate pages `/news` and `/trending`.

Now the author page: app/author/[slug]/page.tsx. Shows avatar, name, role, bio, and their articles. Author JSON-LD (Person) + breadcrumbs.

Let me write it.
Author page.

Now let me build the tools. Three tools:
1. Word Counter (/tools/word-counter) — client component counting words, chars, chars no spaces, sentences, paragraphs, reading time, speaking time, keyword density.
2. Character Counter (/tools/character-counter) — simpler: chars with/without spaces, words, lines.
3. Meta Description Generator (/tools/meta-description-generator) — paste text → generate meta description (simple client-side heuristic: extract first meaningful sentence, title-ish; plus a char counter with 160 limit).

Each tool page is a server page with metadata + a client component. Tools share a layout with breadcrumbs, tools index link, and a "tools nav".

Let me build:
- components/tools/tool-shell.tsx? I'll make a tools layout in app/tools/layout.tsx that wraps with breadcrumbs and a header + tool switcher nav.
- components/tools/word-counter.tsx (client)
- components/tools/character-counter.tsx (client)
- components/tools/meta-description-generator.tsx (client)
- app/tools/page.tsx (index)
- app/tools/word-counter/page.tsx
- app/tools/character-counter/page.tsx
- app/tools/meta-description-generator/page.tsx

Let me first build the word counter client. Counts:
- words: split on whitespace
- characters
- characters (no spaces)
- sentences: count of /[.!?]+/
- paragraphs: split on /\n\s*\n/
- reading time: words/200 wpm
- speaking time: words/130 wpm
- keyword density: top words (excluding stopwords) with percentages

UI: textarea top, stats grid of cards below (mono numbers), keyword density list.

Let me write it.
Now the Free Tools. Building the tools layout + three client-side utilities.

Now the meta description generator. Client-side heuristic approach:
- Input: paste the article text (and optionally a title).
- Generate: 
  - Start with the first sentence (up to ~155 chars), trimmed at sentence boundary.
  - If under ~120 chars, append a value proposition phrase from a small template set using title keywords.
  - If over 160, cut at last sentence boundary before 160.
- Show char count with OK/warn states (150-160 good).
- "Copy" button.
- Allow regenerate (nudge) — I'll generate deterministically but offer a "Nudge" that cycles through template suffixes.

Let me write it.

Now the tool pages + tools index.

app/tools/page.tsx — index with cards linking to each tool.
app/tools/word-counter/page.tsx, etc. with metadata.

Now SEO files: sitemap.ts, robots.ts. Also not-found.tsx, OG default image, and the misc static pages (about, contact, privacy, terms, affiliate-disclosure, login, register).

sitemap.ts: use getAllArticles for article URLs + static pages + categories. Next 16 sitemap function: `export default async function sitemap(): Promise<MetadataRoute.Sitemap>`.

robots.ts: standard.

og-default.png: Next can generate an OG image via `app/opengraph-image.tsx` with ImageResponse. But the brief uses `/og-default.png` referenced in metadata. I can generate a default OG image at build via `opengraph-image.tsx` and keep the metadata reference as the file `og-default.png`? Actually the cleanest: create `app/opengraph-image.tsx` which generates `/opengraph-image` — but my metadata references `/og-default.png`. Let me instead create the default OG image as a static SVG? OG images must be PNG/JPG for most crawlers (Twitter/Facebook don't support SVG). 

Options:
1. Generate `public/og-default.png` via a build script — complex.
2. Use `opengraph-image.tsx` (ImageResponse) at the root — Next auto-adds og:image meta pointing to `/opengraph-image`. Then I don't need the manual `images` entry in metadata. But ImageResponse requires edge runtime support; at build for static pages it runs at request/build time. On Cloudflare OpenNext, ImageResponse may have issues. Also next/font in ImageResponse needs fetch of fonts — network at runtime. Risky for a static Cloudflare deployment.

Simplest robust approach: create the OG default as a real PNG file committed to `public/`. I can generate it with a small Node script using `sharp`? Not installed. I could write an SVG and convert... no converter.

Alternative: use the CoverArt concept but as a static file. I can generate a PNG at build time... Actually, I can write a tiny node script that produces a PNG using pure Node (no deps) — writing a PNG manually is possible but heavy.

Alternative pragmatic approach: keep `og-default.png` in metadata but note it needs to be generated; OR generate a simple PNG via a PowerShell/.NET? Too hacky.

Better: Let me generate the OG image at build time using Next's ImageResponse in `app/opengraph-image.tsx`. When pages are statically generated, Next runs it at build and outputs the file. For Cloudflare Pages static export this works. There's a concern about fonts: I'll use a system font stack in ImageResponse (no network fetch) — default font. Use `fonts: []` and rely on built-in? ImageResponse requires fonts? It uses default sans if not provided? ImageResponse can work without custom fonts (uses a default). Let me check the og image docs quickly.

Actually — simpler and fully deterministic: I'll generate `public/og-default.png` NOW using Node with the `pngjs`? not installed. Hmm.

Let me reconsider: The metadata references `/og-default.png` in three places (layout, article page). If the file doesn't exist, OG tags point to a 404 — bad. So I must provide the file.

Cleanest: use `app/opengraph-image.tsx` with ImageResponse and REMOVE the manual og:image references from metadata (Next injects the generated image automatically). Let me verify ImageResponse works in static builds. It's part of next/og (bundled). At build, for statically rendered routes, Next generates the OG images. This is well-supported. Font: I'll pass `fonts` using local TTFs from node_modules (next/font bundled) — complex. Without custom fonts it uses default. Acceptable for a default OG card; but I'd like the Big Shoulders look. I can load the font files from next/font's dist? The variable font files are downloaded to `.next` at build — not reliably accessible.

Compromise: opengraph-image.tsx with a dark broadcast-style design using system default font weights (400/700). Looks fine.

Also, the brief wants per-article OG images ideally, but "og:image on every article" is satisfied by the default shared image. Good enough for Phase 1; documented as an improvement (generate per-article OG from CoverArt).

So plan:
- Create `app/opengraph-image.tsx` (and maybe `twitter-image.tsx` reusing same) 
- Remove manual `images` in openGraph/twitter from layout.tsx and article page (or keep og-default references removed). Actually Next's file-based opengraph-image overrides the `openGraph.images` metadata? The file convention adds `og:image` with that image. If I also define `openGraph.images`, both could be emitted. I'll remove the manual images to avoid duplicates and rely on the file.

Wait, but twitter card: `twitter:card summary_large_image` + `twitter:images` reference `/og-default.png`. With file-based, Next sets twitter:image too from opengraph-image? I think twitter-image.tsx is separate. If I add `twitter-image.tsx`, Next emits twitter:image. Let me add both opengraph-image.tsx and twitter-image.tsx (same design, sized appropriately: og 1200x630, twitter 1200x630 fine).

Actually, let me simplify: create `app/opengraph-image.tsx` exporting size {1200,630} and alt. And `twitter-image.tsx` same. Remove manual image refs.

Let me also double check ImageResponse availability in Next 16 — import { ImageResponse } from "next/og". Yes, still exists.

Let me verify by reading the metadata-and-og-images doc briefly for the current API (file conventions). Let me grep it.
Now SEO infrastructure. Let me check the Next 16 docs for the current OG-image and sitemap conventions.

AI Tech is an AI and technology news platform built on four engines: live news, evergreen SEO guides, free in-browser tools, and hands-on reviews. The combination is deliberate — a news site lives and dies with the news cycle, so we pair it with content and tools that keep working when the headlines stop moving.

How we cover the news

Stories are written and edited by humans. Where we use AI-assisted drafting, claims are still verified and every article that makes factual assertions links to its{" "} sources. We publish corrections prominently when we get something wrong — it's the only way a fast newsroom keeps its credibility.

  • Sponsored articles — produced in partnership, always labeled.
  • Newsletter sponsorships and (coming later) premium tools.

Wait, `navigator.share` in a client component — during SSR, the component is rendered on the server too (client components are SSR'd). `navigator` is undefined on server. TS lib dom types say navigator is always defined, but at runtime on the server it's undefined → `navigator.share` would throw ReferenceError? # Next.js

Last updated Jun 5, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/framework-guides/web-apps/nextjs/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/)

This is a simple getting started guide. For detailed documentation on how to use the Cloudflare OpenNext adapter, visit the [OpenNext website ↗](https://opennext.js.org/cloudflare).

## What is Next.js?

[Next.js ↗](https://nextjs.org/) is a [React ↗](https://react.dev/) framework for building full stack applications.

Next.js supports Server-side and Client-side rendering, as well as Partial Prerendering which lets you combine static and dynamic components in the same route.

You can deploy your Next.js app to Cloudflare Workers using the OpenNext adapter.

## Next.js supported features

Most Next.js features are supported by the Cloudflare OpenNext adapter:

| Feature                               | Cloudflare adapter  | Notes                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| App Router                            | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Pages Router                          | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Route Handlers                        | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| React Server Components               | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Static Site Generation (SSG)          | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Server-Side Rendering (SSR)           | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Server Actions                        | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Response streaming                    | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| asynchronous work with next/after     | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Middleware                            | 🟢 supported        |                                                                              |
| Image optimization                    | 🟢 supported        | Supported via [Cloudflare Images](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/) |
| Partial Prerendering (PPR)            | 🟢 supported        | PPR is experimental in Next.js                                               |
| Composable Caching ('use cache')      | 🟢 supported        | Composable Caching is experimental in Next.js                                |
| Node.js in Middleware                 | ⚪ not yet supported | Node.js middleware introduced in 15.2 are not yet supported                  |

## Deploy a new Next.js project on Workers

1. **Create a new project with the create-cloudflare CLI (C3).**  
npmyarnpnpm  
```  
npm create cloudflare@latest -- my-next-app --framework=next  
```  
```  
yarn create cloudflare my-next-app --framework=next  
```  
```  
pnpm create cloudflare@latest my-next-app --framework=next  
```  
What's happening behind the scenes?  
When you run this command, C3 creates a new project directory, initiates [Next.js's official setup tool ↗](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app), and configures the project for Cloudflare. It then offers the option to instantly deploy your application to Cloudflare.
2. **Develop locally.**  
After creating your project, run the following command in your project directory to start a local development server. The command uses the Next.js development server. It offers the best developer experience by quickly reloading your app every time the source code is updated.  
npmyarnpnpm  
```  
npm run dev  
```  
```  
yarn run dev  
```  
```  
pnpm run dev  
```
3. **Test and preview your site with the Cloudflare adapter.**  
npmyarnpnpm  
```  
npm run preview  
```  
```  
yarn run preview  
```  
```  
pnpm run preview  
```  
What's the difference between dev and preview?  
The command used in the previous step uses the Next.js development server, which runs in Node.js. However, your deployed application will run on Cloudflare Workers, which uses the `workerd` runtime. Therefore when running integration tests and previewing your application, you should use the preview command, which is more accurate to production, as it executes your application in the `workerd` runtime using `wrangler dev`.
4. **Deploy your project.**  
You can deploy your project to a [\*.workers.dev subdomain](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/workers-dev/) or a [custom domain](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/custom-domains/) from your local machine or any CI/CD system (including [Workers Builds](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/#workers-builds)). ```  
```

```  
```  
pnpm run deploy  
```  
Note  
[**Workers Builds**](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/) requires you to configure environment variables in the ["Build Variables and secrets"](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/configuration/#:~:text=Build%20variables%20and%20secrets) section.  
This ensures the Next build has the necessary access to both public `NEXT_PUBLIC_...` variables and [non-NEXT\_PUBLIC\_... ↗](https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/environment-variables#bundling-environment-variables-for-the-browser), which are essential for tasks like inlining and building SSG pages.  
Learn more in the [OpenNext environment variable guide ↗](https://opennext.js.org/cloudflare/howtos/env-vars#workers-builds)

## Manual configuration

If you prefer to configure your project manually, follow the steps below.

1. **Install [@opennextjs/cloudflare ↗](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opennextjs/cloudflare)**  
npmyarnpnpmbun  
```

2. **Install [wrangler CLI ↗](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler) as a devDependency**  
npmyarnpnpmbun  
```

```  
```

```  
```

```
3. **Add a Wrangler configuration file**  
In your project root, create a [Wrangler configuration file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/) with the following content:  
```jsonc  
{  
	"$schema": "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",  
	"main": ".open-next/worker.js",  
	"name": "my-app",  
	// Set this to today's date  
	"compatibility_date": "2026-08-07",  
	"compatibility_flags": [  
		"nodejs_compat"  
	],  
	"assets": {  
		"directory": ".open-next/assets",  
		"binding": "ASSETS"  
	}  
}  
```  
```toml  
"$schema" = "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json"  
main = ".open-next/worker.js"  
name = "my-app"  
# Set this to today's date  
compatibility_date = "2026-08-07"  
compatibility_flags = [ "nodejs_compat" ]  
[assets]  
directory = ".open-next/assets"  
binding = "ASSETS"  
```  
Note  
As shown above, you must enable the [nodejs\_compat compatibility flag](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/) _and_ set your [compatibility date](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-dates/) to `2024-09-23` or later for your Next.js app to work with @opennextjs/cloudflare.
4. **Add a configuration file for OpenNext**  
In your project root, create an OpenNext configuration file named `open-next.config.ts` with the following content:  
```ts  
import { defineCloudflareConfig } from "@opennextjs/cloudflare";  
export default defineCloudflareConfig();  
```  
Note  
`open-next.config.ts` is where you can configure the caching, see the [adapter documentation ↗](https://opennext.js.org/cloudflare/caching) for more information
5. **Update `package.json`**  
You can add the following scripts to your `package.json`:  
```json  
"preview": "opennextjs-cloudflare build && opennextjs-cloudflare preview",  
"deploy": "opennextjs-cloudflare build && opennextjs-cloudflare deploy",  
"cf-typegen": "wrangler types --env-interface CloudflareEnv cloudflare-env.d.ts"  
```  
Usage

  * `preview`: Builds your app and serves it locally, allowing you to quickly preview your app running locally in the Workers runtime, via a single command.
  * `deploy`: Builds your app, and then deploys it to Cloudflare
  * `cf-typegen`: Generates a `cloudflare-env.d.ts` file at the root of your project containing the types for the env.
6. **Develop locally.**

-- ============================================================
-- AI Tech — Cloudflare D1 (SQLite) schema
-- Phase 2: auth + admin panel + analytics.
-- Apply with:  npx wrangler d1 migrations apply <db> --remote
-- Or migrate to any Postgres (Supabase/Neon) — tables map 1:1.
-- ============================================================

-- ---------- Users & auth ----------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                -- crypto.randomUUID()
  email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  password_hash TEXT,                            -- null for OAuth-only users
  role          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reader'   -- reader | author | editor | admin
    CHECK (role IN ('reader', 'author', 'editor', 'admin')),
  bio           TEXT DEFAULT '',
  avatar_key    TEXT DEFAULT '',
  banned_at     TEXT,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
  updated_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  expires_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  ip            TEXT DEFAULT '',
  user_agent    TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_user ON sessions(user_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verification_tokens (
  identifier    TEXT NOT NULL,
  token         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  expires_at    TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- ---------- Taxonomy ----------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS categories (
  slug        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT DEFAULT '',
  color       TEXT DEFAULT '#3B5BFF',
  position    INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS authors (
  slug       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id    TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  role       TEXT DEFAULT '',
  bio        TEXT DEFAULT '',
  avatar_key TEXT DEFAULT ''
);

-- ---------- Articles ----------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS articles (
  id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  slug           TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  title          TEXT NOT NULL,
  excerpt        TEXT DEFAULT '',
  category_slug  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES categories(slug),
  author_slug    TEXT REFERENCES authors(slug),
  status         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
    CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'scheduled', 'published', 'unpublished')),
  status_tag     TEXT,                          -- live | breaking | updated | trending
  is_featured    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,    -- SQLite boolean
  trending_rank  INTEGER,
  sponsored      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  affiliate_catalog TEXT,                       -- key into affiliate catalog table
  affiliate_disclosed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  content_json   TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- ContentBlock[] (see src/content/types.ts)
  sources_json   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',    -- ArticleSource[]
  image_json     TEXT DEFAULT '{}',             -- ArticleImage
  seo_title      TEXT DEFAULT '',
  seo_description TEXT DEFAULT '',
  published_at   TEXT,
  updated_at     TEXT,
  view_count     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_articles_category ON articles(category_slug, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_articles_published ON articles(status, published_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tags (
  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS article_tags (
  article_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  tag_slug   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tags(slug) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  PRIMARY KEY (article_id, tag_slug)
);

-- ---------- Reader engagement ----------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS saved_articles (
  user_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  article_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, article_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_history (
  id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  article_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  viewed_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reading_history_user ON reading_history(user_id, viewed_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS newsletter_subscribers (
  id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  email     TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  status    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active', 'unsubscribed')),
  source    TEXT DEFAULT '',                    -- home | article | category | sponsor
  locale    TEXT DEFAULT 'en',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS comments (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  article_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id     TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  parent_id   TEXT REFERENCES comments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  body        TEXT NOT NULL,
  status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'hidden')),

input.content:
# Phase 2 — Auth, Admin Panel, Database, Analytics

Phase 1 ships a fully static, SEO-strong news site with zero backend. Phase 2
turns on the editorial machine: accounts, an admin panel, and a real database.

## Goals (from the brief)

1. **Auth** — sign up / log in for readers and staff (email+password first,
   Google/GitHub OAuth after launch). Roles: reader → author → editor → admin.
2. **Admin panel** — manage articles (create/edit/publish/schedule), authors,
   categories, users, and read analytics. Enforced at the auth layer.
3. **Database** — Cloudflare D1 (SQLite) as the primary store; the schema is
   intentionally SQLite-compatible so the same tables can move to Postgres
   (Supabase/Neon) if the project scales out of D1.
4. **Analytics** — first-party pageview tracking (no GA dependency): daily
   pageviews, top articles, countries, devices, referrers. Plus affiliate
   click tracking and newsletter subscriber counts.
5. **Monetization hooks** — write path for the affiliate catalog; affiliate
   clicks attribution table already seeded in the schema.

## Already in place

- `wrangler.jsonc` — Cloudflare Workers config for the OpenNext adapter.
  The Phase 2 `d1_databases` block is documented but commented out; enable it
  and fill the `database_id` (step below).
- `db/schema.sql` — full D1 schema: users, sessions, verification_tokens,
  categories, authors, articles, tags, article_tags, saved_articles,
  reading_history, newsletter_subscribers, comments, pageviews,
  affiliate_clicks, affiliate_products.
- `src/lib/db/auth.ts` — auth seam (`getSession`, `requireAdmin`,
  `isAdminPreview`). Enforced server-side in the admin layout.
- `src/lib/db/repository.ts` — content repository interface + static
  implementation; `src/content/index.ts` already reads through it.
- `src/app/admin/*` — admin shell: dashboard, articles, users, analytics.
  Gated by default; set `AITECH_PHASE2=true` locally to preview.
- Package scripts: `preview` / `deploy` (OpenNext for Cloudflare).

## Roadmap

### 1. Enable D1

```bash
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler d1 create aitech-db        # paste database_id into wrangler.jsonc
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply aitech-db --remote
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply aitech-db --local   # dev
```

Then uncomment the `d1_databases` block in `wrangler.jsonc` and run
`npm run cf-typegen` to regenerate `cloudflare-env.d.ts` (the `DB` binding).

### 2. Auth (Auth.js v5, Credentials + D1)

- Install `next-auth@beta @auth/d1-adapter zod bcryptjs`.
- `src/auth.ts` — Auth.js config: `D1Adapter(env.DB)`, Credentials provider
  verifying `password_hash` (bcrypt), JWT strategy with `role` claim.
- Session cookie: httpOnly, SameSite=lax, 30 days.
- Implement `getSession()` in `src/lib/db/auth.ts` to return the role.
- First admin: seed a `.env` admin, or a one-off
  `npm run seed:admin` script (D1 local + remote).
- Routes: `/login`, `/register` (static shells exist; wire real forms).

### 3. Admin content management

- `GET/POST /api/articles`, `PUT /api/articles/[id]`,
  `DELETE /api/articles/[id]` — route handlers guarded by `requireAdmin`
  (`editor` for writes, `admin` for delete).
- Editor UI on `/admin/articles/[slug]/edit`: blocks map to `ContentBlock[]`
  (`src/content/types.ts`); publish/schedule/draft states stored in
  `articles.status`.
- Wire `/admin/articles` table + dashboard stats to the D1 repository.
- Swap `src/lib/db/repository.ts` to the D1 implementation — templates
  unchanged (they already consume the same interface).

### 4. Analytics pipeline

- `POST /api/v` — client beacon (pageview, locale, referrer, device via UA
  bucket, country via `CF-IPCountry` header). Written to `pageviews`.
- Admin `/admin/analytics` — daily totals, top articles, countries, devices.
- Affiliate clicks: `POST /api/affiliate/click` → `affiliate_clicks`.
- Newsletter: replace the local-storage MVP with a provider API + store
  rows in `newsletter_subscribers`.

### 5. Users & moderation

- `/admin/users` — list users, change roles, ban (sets `banned_at`;
  `getSession` rejects banned users).
- Comments moderation (`comments.status`), spam flags.

## Data layer contract

`src/lib/db/repository.ts` defines `ContentRepository`:

- `getArticles(): Article[]`
- `getAuthors(): Author[]`
- `getCategories(): Category[]`
- `getAffiliateProducts(catalog?: string): AffiliateProductData[]`

The D1 implementation returns rows mapped to the same `Article`/`Author`/
`Category` types (`src/content/types.ts`), so pages stay untouched. Prefer
generated column accessors over `env.DB.prepare()` inline queries.

## Conventions

- **Server-only auth**: every `/admin` route and API handler checks the
  session at the server. Never gate by hiding UI alone.
- **Secrets**: `AUTH_SECRET`, OAuth keys, DB credentials live in Cloudflare
  Variables (or `.dev.vars` for local), never in the repo. `.env*` is gitignored.
- **Build checks**: `npm run lint` then `npm run build` before any admin
  feature ships; `npm run preview` verifies the Cloudflare bundle.

# AI Tech — AI & Tech News Platform

A broadcast-styled technology news and tools site built with Next.js 16
(App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind v4, and deployed to **Cloudflare
(Workers/Pages)** via the OpenNext adapter.

- **Phase 1 (done):** fully static, SEO-strong public site — live feeds,
  trending, categories, articles, comparison tables, affiliate disclosure,
  free client-side tools, sitemap/robots/OG images.
- **Phase 2 (in progress):** auth, admin panel, D1 database, first-party
  analytics. Plan: [`docs/phase-2.md`](docs/phase-2.md).

## Local development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Phase 1 needs no environment variables. `.env.example` documents Phase 2+
variables (auth secret, database, analytics).

## Scripts

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Next.js dev server (localhost:3000) |
| `npm run build` | Production build (Turbopack) |
| `npm run start` | Serve the production build |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |
| `npm run preview` | OpenNext build + local Cloudflare preview (Wrangler) |
| `npm run deploy` | OpenNext build + deploy to Cloudflare Workers |
| `npm run cf-typegen` | Regenerate `cloudflare-env.d.ts` from `wrangler.jsonc` |

## Deployment (Cloudflare)

This project deploys as a Cloudflare Worker with static assets, using the
OpenNext for Cloudflare adapter. Configure once:

```bash
npx wrangler login
npm run deploy
```

For previews against the Cloudflare runtime:

```bash
npm run preview
```

Notes:

- `wrangler.jsonc` — worker entry (`.open-next/worker.js`), assets binding,
  `nodejs_compat` compatibility flag.
- Phase 2 database (D1): create `aitech-db`, paste its `database_id` into
  the `d1_databases` block, apply migrations. See `docs/phase-2.md`.
- Secrets (e.g. `AUTH_SECRET`) are stored as Cloudflare Variables / Secrets —
  never committed. Local equivalents go in `.dev.vars`.

## Project structure

```
src/
  app/                 # App Router pages
    [category]/        # category + article routes
    admin/             # Phase 2 admin panel (gated)
    tools/             # free in-browser tools
  components/          # UI: hero, cards, article renderer, ad slots…
  content/             # Phase 1 data layer (articles, authors, categories)
  lib/                 # site config, i18n, utils
  lib/db/              # Phase 2 seams: repository + auth
docs/phase-2.md        # Phase 2 roadmap (auth, admin, D1, analytics)
db/schema.sql          # D1 schema
wrangler.jsonc         # Cloudflare deployment config
open-next.config.ts    # OpenNext adapter config
```

## Content model

Articles are typed, block-based content (`src/content/types.ts`). Phase 1
ships them as static data; Phase 2 stores the same shape in D1
(`db/schema.sql`, `articles.content_json`) and swaps the repository in
`src/lib/db/repository.ts` — templates don't change.

## Admin (Phase 2 preview)

The admin panel is server-gated. Without auth it shows a lock screen. To
preview the shell locally set `AITECH_PHASE2=true` in `.env.local` (never in
production — it bypasses the gate).

400 Bad Request on login via curl with the same JSON. Interesting — with Invoke-RestMethod it worked (200). The difference: PowerShell's ConvertTo-Json vs my inline JSON string. My inline `'{"email":"admin@aitech.media","password":"Admin2026!"}'` — in curl on Windows, the single quotes are part of the shell? In cmd/PowerShell, `curl.exe -d '...'` passes the single quotes literally to curl! PowerShell doesn't strip single quotes for native command args — it does actually treat them as quoting, but historically there are quirks with quotes being passed to native executables. The JSON likely got mangled with literal quotes passed incorrectly.

Actually PowerShell 5.1 has the famous native argument passing issue: it may pass the single-quoted string without the quotes, but then curl receives `-d {email:admin@...}` without quotes → invalid JSON → 400. That's why.

Solution: use escaped double quotes inside PowerShell: `"{""email"":""admin@aitech.media"",""password"":""Admin2026!""}"` or use `--data-raw`. Simpler: use a here-string variable and pass via curl with proper quoting. In PowerShell:

```
$json = '{"email":"admin@aitech.media","password":"Admin2026!"}'
curl.exe -v -c ... -d $json ...
```

PowerShell passes `$json` as a single argument containing the JSON string (no shell quoting issues since it's an argument variable). curl receives `-d {"email":"..."}` as one arg — curl treats it as the data string. That works.

display.text:
# Phase 2 — Auth, Admin Panel, Database, Analytics

Phase 1 ships a fully static, SEO-strong news site with zero backend. Phase 2
turns on the editorial machine: accounts, an admin panel, and a real database.

## Goals (from the brief)

1. **Auth** — sign up / log in for readers and staff (email+password first,
   Google/GitHub OAuth after launch). Roles: reader → author → editor → admin.
2. **Admin panel** — manage articles (create/edit/publish/schedule), authors,
   categories, users, and read analytics. Enforced at the auth layer.
3. **Database** — Cloudflare D1 (SQLite) as the primary store; the schema is
   intentionally SQLite-compatible so the same tables can move to Postgres
   (Supabase/Neon) if the project scales out of D1.
4. **Analytics** — first-party pageview tracking (no GA dependency): daily
   pageviews, top articles, countries, devices, referrers. Plus affiliate
   click tracking and newsletter subscriber counts.
5. **Monetization hooks** — write path for the affiliate catalog; affiliate
   clicks attribution table already seeded in the schema.

## Already in place

- `wrangler.jsonc` — Cloudflare Workers config for the OpenNext adapter with
  the `DB` D1 binding **enabled** (works locally now; replace the placeholder
  `database_id` before remote deploy).
- `db/migrations/0001_schema.sql` — full D1 schema: users, sessions,
  verification_tokens, categories, authors, articles, tags, article_tags,
  saved_articles, reading_history, newsletter_subscribers, comments,
  pageviews, affiliate_clicks, affiliate_products. **Already applied locally**.
- `src/lib/db/auth.ts` — auth seam (`getSession`, `requireAdmin`,
  `isAdminPreview`). Enforced server-side in the admin layout.
- `src/lib/db/repository.ts` — content repository interface + static
  implementation; `src/content/index.ts` already reads through it.
- `src/app/admin/*` — admin shell: dashboard, articles, users, analytics.
  Gated by default; set `AITECH_PHASE2=true` locally to preview.
- Package scripts: `preview` / `deploy` (OpenNext for Cloudflare).

## Roadmap

### 1. Enable D1 (local ✓, remote pending)

Local is already wired: the `DB` binding is active in `wrangler.jsonc`, the
schema is applied to the local database, and `cloudflare-env.d.ts` types the
`DB` binding (`npm run cf-typegen` to regenerate).

For the remote database:

```bash
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler d1 create aitech-db        # paste database_id into wrangler.jsonc
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply aitech-db --remote
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply aitech-db --local   # dev (already done)
```

Then uncomment the `d1_databases` block in `wrangler.jsonc` and run
`npm run cf-typegen` to regenerate `cloudflare-env.d.ts` (the `DB` binding).

### 2. Auth (Auth.js v5, Credentials + D1)

- Install `next-auth@beta @auth/d1-adapter zod bcryptjs`.
- `src/auth.ts` — Auth.js config: `D1Adapter(env.DB)`, Credentials provider
  verifying `password_hash` (bcrypt), JWT strategy with `role` claim.
- Session cookie: httpOnly, SameSite=lax, 30 days.
- Implement `getSession()` in `src/lib/db/auth.ts` to return the role.
- First admin: seed a `.env` admin, or a one-off
  `npm run seed:admin` script (D1 local + remote).
- Routes: `/login`, `/register` (static shells exist; wire real forms).

### 3. Admin content management

- `GET/POST /api/articles`, `PUT /api/articles/[id]`,
  `DELETE /api/articles/[id]` — route handlers guarded by `requireAdmin`
  (`editor` for writes, `admin` for delete).
- Editor UI on `/admin/articles/[slug]/edit`: blocks map to `ContentBlock[]`
  (`src/content/types.ts`); publish/schedule/draft states stored in
  `articles.status`.
- Wire `/admin/articles` table + dashboard stats to the D1 repository.
- Swap `src/lib/db/repository.ts` to the D1 implementation — templates
  unchanged (they already consume the same interface).

### 4. Analytics pipeline

- `POST /api/v` — client beacon (pageview, locale, referrer, device via UA
  bucket, country via `CF-IPCountry` header). Written to `pageviews`.
- Admin `/admin/analytics` — daily totals, top articles, countries, devices.
- Affiliate clicks: `POST /api/affiliate/click` → `affiliate_clicks`.
- Newsletter: replace the local-storage MVP with a provider API + store
  rows in `newsletter_subscribers`.

### 5. Users & moderation

- `/admin/users` — list users, change roles, ban (sets `banned_at`;
  `getSession` rejects banned users).
- Comments moderation (`comments.status`), spam flags.

## Data layer contract

`src/lib/db/repository.ts` defines `ContentRepository`:

- `getArticles(): Article[]`
- `getAuthors(): Author[]`
- `getCategories(): Category[]`
- `getAffiliateProducts(catalog?: string): AffiliateProductData[]`

The D1 implementation returns rows mapped to the same `Article`/`Author`/
`Category` types (`src/content/types.ts`), so pages stay untouched. Prefer
generated column accessors over `env.DB.prepare()` inline queries.

## Conventions

- **Server-only auth**: every `/admin` route and API handler checks the
  session at the server. Never gate by hiding UI alone.
- **Secrets**: `AUTH_SECRET`, OAuth keys, DB credentials live in Cloudflare
  Variables (or `.dev.vars` for local), never in the repo. `.env*` is gitignored.
- **Build checks**: `npm run lint` then `npm run build` before any admin
  feature ships; `npm run preview` verifies the Cloudflare bundle.

  (`src/content/types.ts`); publish/schedule/draft states stored in
  `articles.status`.
- Wire `/admin/articles` table + dashboard stats to the D1 repository.
- Swap `src/lib/db/repository.ts` to the D1 implementation — templates
  unchanged (they already consume the same interface).

### 3. Analytics pipeline

- `POST /api/v` — client beacon (pageview, locale, referrer, device via UA
  bucket, country via `CF-IPCountry` header). Written to `pageviews`.
- Admin `/admin/analytics` — daily totals, top articles, countries, devices.
- Affiliate clicks: `POST /api/affiliate/click` → `affiliate_clicks`.
- Newsletter: replace the local-storage MVP with a provider API + store
  rows in `newsletter_subscribers`.

### 4. Users & moderation

- `/admin/users` — change roles, ban (sets `banned_at`; `getSession` rejects
  banned users).
- Comments moderation (`comments.status`), spam flags.

`src/lib/db/repository.ts` defines `ContentRepository`:

- `getArticles(): Article[]`
- `getAuthors(): Author[]`
- `getCategories(): Category[]`
- `getAffiliateProducts(catalog?: string): AffiliateProductData[]`

`Category` types (`src/content/types.ts`), so pages stay untouched. Prefer
generated column accessors over `env.DB.prepare()` inline queries.

- **Server-only auth**: every `/admin` route and API handler checks the
  session at the server. Never gate by hiding UI alone.
- **Secrets**: `AUTH_SECRET`, OAuth keys, DB credentials live in Cloudflare
  Variables (or `.dev.vars` / `.env` for local), never in the repo.
  `.env*` and `.dev.vars` are gitignored.
- **Build checks**: `npm run lint` then `npm run build` before any feature
  ships; `npm run preview` verifies the Cloudflare bundle.

For previews against the Cloudflare runtime:

```bash
npm run preview
```

Notes:

- `wrangler.jsonc` — worker entry (`.open-next/worker.js`), assets binding,
  `nodejs_compat` compatibility flag.
- Phase 2 database (D1): create `aitech-db`, paste its `database_id` into

- Secrets (e.g. `AUTH_SECRET`) are stored as Cloudflare Variables / Secrets —
  never committed. Local equivalents go in `.dev.vars`.

## Project structure

```
src/
  app/                 # App Router pages
    [category]/        # category + article routes
    admin/             # Phase 2 admin panel (gated)
    tools/             # free in-browser tools
  components/          # UI: hero, cards, article renderer, ad slots…
  content/             # Phase 1 data layer (articles, authors, categories)
  lib/                 # site config, i18n, utils
  lib/db/              # Phase 2 seams: repository + auth
docs/phase-2.md        # Phase 2 roadmap (auth, admin, D1, analytics)
db/migrations/          # D1 migrations (0001_schema.sql)
wrangler.jsonc         # Cloudflare deployment config
open-next.config.ts    # OpenNext adapter config
```

## Content model

Articles are typed, block-based content (`src/content/types.ts`). Phase 1
ships them as static data; Phase 2 stores the same shape in D1
(`db/migrations`, `articles.content_json`) and swaps the repository in
`src/lib/db/repository.ts` — templates don't change.

## Admin (Phase 2 preview)

The admin panel is server-gated. Without auth it shows a lock screen. To
preview the shell locally set `AITECH_PHASE2=true` in `.env.local` (never in
production — it bypasses the gate).

## License

Private project. All rights reserved.

## Admin (Phase 2)

The admin panel is server-gated at the auth layer: signed-out visitors see a
sign-in screen, non-admins are redirected home. Register an account, then
promote it to admin by seeding:

```bash
npm run seed:admin                  # admin@aitech.media / Admin2026!
npm run seed:admin -- you@site.com pass
```

Local dev writes straight to `.data/local.sqlite` (plain Node) or the local
D1 store under `wrangler dev`. Before deploying to Cloudflare, seed the
remote database too:

```bash
npx wrangler d1 execute aitech-db --remote --file=db/seeds/admin.sql
```

Set `AUTH_SECRET` (see `.env.example`) in production — without it the local
dev fallback secret is used, which is unsafe on a public site.

This affects static generation: the homepage would then hit the DB at build and become dynamic (or at least non-cacheable... actually RSC caching: with dynamic API used it becomes dynamic; but it just awaits getDbArticles → in Node build it falls back to local sqlite, so it stays a prerendered static page but includes DB content at build time — not live for remote D1).

Hmm, important trade-off: on Cloudflare, `next build` prerenders pages. If homepage awaits getDbArticles, at build time it uses local sqlite (or fails). That means CMS content is baked at build → new articles won't appear until rebuild. To make them appear live, the homepage must be dynamic (force-dynamic) so it reads D1 per request.

The user's goal: "new articles show breaking on top immediately after creating." That requires the homepage to be dynamic (per-request DB read). In wrangler dev, everything is dynamic anyway.

Options:
- Convert homepage to async + use getSite* helpers + set `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (or `revalidate = 0`). This makes homepage live but loses static caching.

Given the whole site is a CMS-driven news site, making the homepage dynamic is reasonable. But it's a bigger architectural decision. The user said earlier we built SSG static content with D1 layer for CMS. The natural next step is the homepage reads merged content dynamically.

Let me convert homepage to async with site getters and force-dynamic. Actually, better to keep it simple and aligned: use `export const revalidate = 0`? In Next 15+, `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` is the clean way. With `getCloudflareContext()` in getDB, in Cloudflare it's request-scoped; in Node (next dev without wrangler) it falls back to local sqlite.

But there's a catch: HomePage currently also feeds `getAllArticles()` to LiveStats (counts). I'll keep sync getAllArticles for counts, and use getSite* for lists.

On Windows, curl needs double quotes escaped.

    color: "#4AD2A6",
  },
];

const bySlug = new Map<CategorySlug, Category>(categories.map((c) => [c.slug, c]));

export function getCategory(slug: string): Category | undefined {
  return bySlug.get(slug as CategorySlug);
}

export function getCategoryBySlug(slug: CategorySlug): Category {
  const c = bySlug.get(slug);
  if (!c) throw new Error(`Unknown category: ${slug}`);
  return c;
}

TechHow is a how-to site for everyday computer problems. Windows, macOS, hardware, software, internet, security, coding and AI — written in plain English, tested on a clean machine, and updated when the steps change.

How we write

Every guide starts with a real problem someone asked us to solve. We reproduce it, work through the fix, and write the steps so a beginner can follow them the first time. Where a guide has multiple routes, we pick the safest and tell you why.

How we make money

  • Affiliate links in product picks — always disclosed, never behind the verdict.
  • Sponsored articles — produced in partnership, always labeled.
  • Newsletter and (coming later) premium tool tiers.

None of it changes a recommendation. We only recommend software and hardware we have actually installed and used.

Corrections

Guides age — operating systems change. When a reader spots a step that no longer works, we test it and update the guide, marking the change. Corrections are welcome:{" "} hello@techhow.example.

); }
