This is a big redesign. The design philosophy currently is "dark broadcast/control-room" — but the site is a how-to tutorial site. The user wants "light and modern, clean (Linear/Stripe style)".

Let me plan the full redesign concretely. I'll change the theme to light-first with a clean modern aesthetic while keeping the same component structure (to minimize risk). Key changes:

**1. Design tokens (globals.css):**
- Make light the default (`:root` = light palette), `.dark` override = current dark palette.
- Softer accent: keep blue #3b5bff as primary but maybe refine. For a clean Linear/Stripe look: white bg #ffffff, near-black fg #0f1117, muted slate grays, hairline borders rgba, accent indigo #5B5BD6 / #4F46E5 or keep #3B5BFF. Let me use a refined indigo: #5A4BDA or #4F46E5. Actually Linear uses #5E6AD2. Let me use `--signal: #5b5bd6`? Hmm. Let me go with a modern indigo/violet: `#6E56CF` (Radix) or `#4F46E5` (indigo-600). I'll pick `#4F46E5` for a crisp modern feel. Signal-ink (links on light) → `#4338CA`.
- Amber → `#F59E0B` (amber-500) refined.
- Typography: For clean modern, replace Big Shoulders (condensed uppercase broadcast font) with "Space Grotesk" for display (modern, geometric, techy but clean) — not uppercase necessarily. Actually the `.font-display` class applies `text-transform: uppercase`. For a clean modern look, uppercase condensed headlines feel "broadcast". I should remove the forced uppercase for a modern look. But that requires touching many components that rely on `.font-display` + uppercase classes (they use `uppercase` in className anyway). Hmm, components use `font-display text-4xl font-extrabold uppercase`. If I change `.font-display` to Space Grotesk and keep uppercase, it still looks techy but cleaner. Space Grotesk uppercase is fine. Let me keep the structure but swap the font to Space Grotesk, and tone down letter-spacing. Actually for Linear/Stripe style, sentence-case headings look more modern. But removing `uppercase` everywhere is a big refactor. 

Let me be strategic: The `.font-display` utility applies uppercase + line-height 0.95. I can override it: use Space Grotesk, remove forced uppercase in the utility, and let components keep their own `uppercase` classes where appropriate (nav labels, kickers — those should stay mono uppercase for the "clean editorial" look). For big headings, many components pass `uppercase` in className explicitly (hero h1, section titles, page titles). Sentence-case would be nicer but the uppercase still looks decent with Space Grotesk. 

Hmm, but the user wants a noticeably different design. The biggest visual signals of the current design:
1. Dark navy + blue circuit/PCB aesthetic → change to light.
2. Big condensed uppercase display font → Space Grotesk (still uppercase is okay-ish) — but honestly for "clean modern" I'd go sentence case. Let me do a moderate approach: change font-display to Space Grotesk and remove the uppercase/text-transform from the utility so headings inherit component classes. Then strip explicit `uppercase` from the main heading components (hero, section-heading, article page, category page, static page, article-card). Kickers/nav stay mono uppercase.

Actually, let me reconsider scope. A full redesign across ~30 components is risky but the user explicitly asked "промениш целия дизайн" (change the whole design). I'll do it properly.

**Plan of files to change:**

Design system:
- `globals.css`: light-first tokens, dark override, softer shadows, refined status dots, keep utility classes.
- `layout.tsx`: swap Big_Shoulders → Space_Grotesk; update THEME_SCRIPT for light default (add `.dark` only if stored "dark"). themeColor update.
- `theme-toggle.tsx`: flip default to light; toggle `.dark` class; icons swap (default shows moon since light default; when dark, show sun). Actually the toggle should: if not dark → show moon (click to go dark). So invert logic.

Components (big visual ones):
- `header.tsx`: clean white header — remove breaking strip (or make subtle), add account menu (session-aware), adjust logo text.
- `hero.tsx`: clean editorial hero — light, simpler. Featured story with white card, soft shadow, cover art, no dark overlay gradient (or light gradient).
- `ticker.tsx`: remove marquee broadcast or replace with a clean "Latest" strip. I'll replace with a simple static latest-articles strip (no animation) — cleaner. Or remove entirely from home. Simpler: restyle as a clean horizontal scroll list without amber "Breaking" label. Let me make it a clean border strip with subtle "New" badge.
- `cover-art.tsx`: adapt from navy broadcast to light clean — soft light background, subtle gradient, accent color, keep label. This is the biggest visual piece (used everywhere).
- `article-card.tsx`: clean cards, rounded, soft border/shadow, remove dark overlaid text? Currently cards use CoverArt with text overlay. Let me check article-card.tsx.
- `footer.tsx`: clean light footer.
- `live-stats.tsx`: keep but light (works with tokens automatically). Maybe rename "Signal feed" → fine. Actually the design change mainly comes from tokens. The components that hardcode dark colors need manual fixes.
- `category-preview.tsx`, `section-heading.tsx`, `breadcrumbs.tsx`, `status-tag.tsx`, `ad-slot.tsx`, `search-dialog.tsx`, `mobile-nav.tsx`, `newsletter.tsx`, `circuit-divider.tsx` — check for hardcoded dark colors.

Given the scale, let me approach with a subagent? No — the subagent might not follow my design intent precisely. Let me do it myself but efficiently. I'll focus on:

1. Design tokens light-first (globals.css) + fonts (layout.tsx) + theme toggle — this single change flips the whole site to light/clean automatically since all components use CSS vars. 
2. Fix components with hardcoded dark colors: hero (uses black/white overlays), cover-art (hardcoded navy), code-block (hardcoded dark), ticker (amber/black), ad-slot fine, mobile-nav uses bg-bg (fine), article-card overlay (uses bg-bg/80, fine; text might be white on image).
3. Header account menu + session awareness.
4. Account page.

Let me check which components hardcode colors by grepping for white, black, #1..., #0d0e16 etc.

Let me also reconsider fonts: Space Grotesk for display + keep Inter + IBM Plex Mono. Space Grotesk is on Google Fonts via next/font/google. Good.

Actually, for a truly "Linear/Stripe" clean look, maybe I should NOT use uppercase headlines. Let me remove `text-transform: uppercase` from `.font-display` and update key headings to sentence case by removing their `uppercase` classes. Let me grep for `font-display.*uppercase` occurrences and handle the main ones. Actually many. Let me instead keep uppercase OFF in the utility and remove `uppercase` from headings in these components: hero.tsx h1, page.tsx (home sections use SectionHeading + h2), section-heading.tsx, article page h1, category page h1, static-page h1, article-card h3, category-preview h2, trending page, news/tutorials page h1, admin pages h1. Kickers and small labels stay mono uppercase.

This is a lot of edits. Let me be efficient with a plan and execute.

Let me first check the remaining components for hardcoded colors: search-dialog, mobile-nav (done), article-card, category-preview, section-heading, breadcrumbs, circuit-divider, share-buttons, sources-block, newsletter (fine), author page, admin pages.

Let me read article-card, category-preview, section-heading, breadcrumbs, circuit-divider, search-dialog.
Това е голям редизайн. Чета останалите компоненти, за да видя твърдо закодираните тъмни цветове.

26: /** Mulberry32 — tiny deterministic PRNG so art is stable per seed. */
27: function mulberry32(seed: number) {
28:   let a = seed >>> 0;
29:   return () => {
30:     a |= 0;
31:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0;
32:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
33:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
34:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
35:   };
36: }
37: 
38: function hashString(str: string): number {
39:   let h = 2166136261;
40:   for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
41:     h ^= str.charCodeAt(i);
42:     h = Math.imul(h, 16777619);
43:   }
44:   return h >>> 0;
45: }
46: 
47: function Traces({ seed, accent }: { seed: string; accent: string }) {
48:   const rnd = mulberry32(hashString(seed) ^ 0x9e3779b9);
49:   const traces: React.ReactNode[] = [];
50:   const W = 1200;
51:   const H = 630;
52:   for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
53:     const startX = Math.round(rnd() * W);
54:     const startY = Math.round(rnd() * H);
55:     const segments = 2 + Math.floor(rnd() * 3);
56:     let x = startX;
57:     let y = startY;
58:     let d = `M${x} ${y}`;
59:     for (let s = 0; s < segments; s++) {
60:       if (rnd() > 0.5) {
61:         x += Math.round((rnd() - 0.2) * 260);
62:       } else {
63:         y += Math.round((rnd() - 0.2) * 260);
64:       }
65:       d += ` L${Math.max(0, Math.min(W, x))} ${Math.max(0, Math.min(H, y))}`;
66:     }
67:     traces.push(

69:         <path d={d} fill="none" stroke={accent} strokeOpacity={0.16} strokeWidth={2} />
70:         <circle cx={Math.max(0, Math.min(W, x))} cy={Math.max(0, Math.min(H, y))} r={5} fill={accent} fillOpacity={0.35} />
71:       </g>,
72:     );
73:   }
74:   return <>{traces}</>;

parts.text: "Invalid request body" — my JSON escaping is probably off. The `-d '{\"email\":...}'` in PowerShell — backslash-escaping double quotes inside single quotes isn't how it works. In PowerShell, single-quoted strings are verbatim, so `{\"email\"...}` sends literal backslashes. Earlier in the conversation curl tests worked — maybe they used a different quoting. Let me use a proper JSON with PowerShell escaping: use double-quoted string with backtick-escaped quotes, or write JSON to a temp file and use `-d @file`. Simplest: write body to a temp file.

2: import path from "node:path";
3: import { DatabaseSync, type SQLInputValue } from "node:sqlite";
4: import type { DBLike, DBPrepared } from "./client";
5: 
6: /**
7:  * Local dev database for plain-Node Next.js (`npm run dev` / `next start`),
8:  * where no Cloudflare binding exists. Uses the built-in `node:sqlite`
9:  * (Node ≥ 22.5) against `.data/local.sqlite`, bootstrapped from the same
10:  * migration file the production D1 database uses — so schema stays in sync.
11:  */
12: 
13: const DATA_DIR = path.join(process.cwd(), ".data");
14: const DB_FILE = path.join(DATA_DIR, "local.sqlite");
15: const MIGRATIONS_DIR = path.join(process.cwd(), "db", "migrations");
16: 
17: let db: DatabaseSync | null = null;
18: 
19: /** Applies every migration in db/migrations that hasn't run yet (tracked in
20:  * `_migrations`), keeping the local SQLite file in sync with D1. */
21: export function runMigrations(handle: DatabaseSync) {
22:   handle.exec(
23:     "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _migrations (name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')))",
24:   );
25:   const applied = new Set(
26:     handle.prepare("SELECT name FROM _migrations").all().map((r) => (r as { name: string }).name),
27:   );
28:   if (!existsSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)) return;
29:   const files = readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".sql")).sort();
30:   const insert = handle.prepare("INSERT INTO _migrations (name) VALUES (?)");
31:   for (const file of files) {
32:     if (applied.has(file)) continue;
33:     handle.exec(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, file), "utf8"));
34:     insert.run(file);
35:   }
36: }
37: 
38: function open(): DatabaseSync {
39:   if (db) return db;
40: 
41:   if (!existsSync(DATA_DIR)) mkdirSync(DATA_DIR, { recursive: true });
42: 
43:   const handle = new DatabaseSync(DB_FILE);
44:   handle.exec("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;");
45:   runMigrations(handle);
46: 
47:   db = handle;
48:   return handle;
49: }

51: class SqlitePrepared implements DBPrepared {
52:   private params: unknown[] = [];
53: 
54:   constructor(private sql: string) {}
55: 
56:   bind(...values: unknown[]): this {
57:     this.params = values;
58:     return this;
59:   }
60: 
61:   async first<T = Record<string, unknown>>(): Promise<T | null> {
62:     const row = open().prepare(this.sql).get(...(this.params as SQLInputValue[])) as T | undefined;
63:     return row ?? null;
64:   }
65: 
66:   async all<T = Record<string, unknown>>(): Promise<{ results: T[] }> {
67:     const results = open().prepare(this.sql).all(...(this.params as SQLInputValue[])) as T[];
68:     return { results };
69:   }
70: 
71:   async run(): Promise<{ success: boolean; meta?: unknown }> {
72:     const meta = open().prepare(this.sql).run(...(this.params as SQLInputValue[]));
73:     return { success: true, meta };
74:   }
75: }

82:     },
